apiAdaptationNotes: The Figma Form page is still marked work-in-progress (🚧). The <form-row> column gap was initially unset (0); it has since been set to --spacing-lg (16px) in Figma, matching what the code already used, so it is no longer a judgment call. One call remains: the header title is a Figma text node, so `title` renders as presentational text, not a semantic heading.
Figma's `sections` variant (1/2/3) is not a prop - it is just however many FormSection children the consumer renders.

The <form-header> is always the form's own header, so it is baked into Form (title/description/requiredLegend props) rather than a separate export. The description's '* indicates a required field' legend is exposed as the `requiredLegend` boolean, rendering the '*' in --color-content-error to match Field's required marker.
Multi-part component shipped as four separate exports (Form, FormSection, FormRow, FormFooter), matching the repo's Tabs/TabPanel and RadioGroup/Radio pattern rather than dot-notation compounds.
All inter-block spacing lives on the blocks (section padding-top 3xl, footer padding-top 4xl); the <form> has no gap of its own, so a header-less form has no wasted leading space.

Fields may sit directly in a FormSection (single column, spaced by the section gap) or inside a FormRow (equal columns) - Figma always nests rows in sections, but the direct-field case is the common one and avoids a mandatory one-slot row.
Form owns no form state - it renders a native <form> and forwards onSubmit and all native form attributes; validation and each field's state stay native / on Field.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.description: Bordered frame holding the optional before/action slots and the input; reacts to :hover, :focus-within, and the input's :autofill (via :has).

anatomy.name: iconBefore
anatomy.description: Optional leading icon or short text prefix. Always decorative - never interactive.

anatomy.name: leadingContent
anatomy.description: Optional interactive in-frame content before the input, sharing its row - added so a token/multi-select field (Select) can render removable chips inside the frame. Shrinks and clips to keep the field single-line. Unlike iconBefore, not aria-hidden.

anatomy.name: input
anatomy.description: The real native text input; carries all forwarded native attributes.

anatomy.name: iconAfter
anatomy.description: Optional trailing icon or interactive action (e.g. an IconButton clear button). Never forced aria-hidden.

size.description: Frame height, padding, gap, and typography.

context.description: default is bordered at rest, rounded on all four corners; inline has no border/background at rest, shows the raised-hover background and a 1px bottom border on hover, a 2px bottom focus/error line on focus/invalid, and always has square bottom corners - for a field inside a row, such as a search box or a Key Value Pair value. Matches Figma's context axis.

appearance.description: Deprecated - use context. subtle and inline map to context='inline', default to 'default'. Still accepted; an explicit context wins.

invalid.description: Sets aria-invalid and the error border (thicker, regardless of focus).

iconBefore.description: Optional leading icon or short text prefix. Always decorative (aria-hidden).

iconAfter.description: Optional trailing icon or interactive control (typically an IconButton clear action, or a Button). Never forced aria-hidden.

className.description: Composes with the root frame's class list.

inputClassName.description: Composes with the native input's class list.

leadingContent.description: Interactive in-frame content between iconBefore and the input (e.g. Select's chips). Not aria-hidden; shrinks/clips to stay single-line. Existing usage is unchanged when omitted.

color.autofill_background: --color-background-autofill-default layered over --color-elevation-surface-raised-default (context=default unless hovered; context=inline only while focused)

requirements: Render a real native <input> - never fake one.
Set aria-invalid on the input when invalid is true.
iconBefore is aria-hidden - decorative only, never interactive.
iconAfter is never forced aria-hidden - it may hold a real interactive control (e.g. an IconButton clear action) which must keep its own accessible name and stay keyboard-reachable.
Text Field does not manage labelling - pair with a native label[htmlFor] or aria-label/aria-labelledby.

showCaret.note: Figma mockup-only, not a real prop.

placeholder.note: Figma mockup-only toggle between placeholder/value text, not a real prop.

elemBeforeInputComponent.note: Separate Figma component for the leading slot. Never interactive. The text case (e.g. a '$' currency prefix) is bound to fixed body-lg typography at every field size.

elemAfterInputComponent.note: Separate Figma component for the trailing slot. Frequently interactive (e.g. a clear action) - confirmed from a screenshot of the clear icon-button in its hover state. The icon-button case uses appearance=subtle, shape=square. A third `label` type was added later, nesting a real Label atom instance (tone=default, emphasis=subtle) for compact metadata/status after the input (e.g. a unit or status pill) - confirmed directly from the component's own nested instance properties, not assumed. iconAfter is already typed React.ReactNode and .action is a plain centered flex wrapper, so a Label already renders correctly there with no component code changes.

apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's autofill state (added after this contract was first written; re-checked 2026-10-13 in both contexts) layers color/background/autofill/default (raised from 8% to 16% opacity on 2026-10-14, in the Tokens file and code: prussian/alpha/900/16 light, 500/16 dark) over color/elevation/surface/raised/default on context=default, keeping its border/input 1px stroke. context=inline's autofill variants have no fill or stroke, the same as inline filled (their two fills were removed on 2026-10-14, per design feedback). Code applies it as one background shorthand (the tint layered over raised-default) when the input matches :autofill, or under the documentation-only data-force-state='autofill' pin, except when disabled. Figma shows autofill only on its own; per explicit design feedback (2026-10-14), code settles the combinations a browser produces two ways. Hover replaces the tint: the hover rules outrank the autofill rule and set the background shorthand, which clears it; focus and invalid change only the border, so the tint stays. context=inline stays chromeless at rest, as Figma's inline autofill variant does, and shows the tint only while focused, which Figma doesn't draw. The browser's own !important autofill fill on the input is hidden with background-clip: text, and -webkit-text-fill-color/caret-color replace its forced text color. Not a long background-color transition: that needs a raw timing the motion rules don't allow, and switching it off for reduced motion would bring the browser's fill back. Not an inset box-shadow in the frame color either: that would have to follow every frame state.

Figma's 'state' axis (default/hover/focus/typing/filled/autofill) is not a real prop - verified from bound tokens: hover=:hover, focus=focus+empty (:focus-within + :placeholder-shown), typing=focus+has-value (:focus-within, not :placeholder-shown), filled=unfocused+has-value (not :placeholder-shown), autofill=:autofill on the input. All five derive from native pseudo-classes plus the input's own value; none are exposed as a prop.

Figma's 'context' axis (default/inline) is the 'context' prop - the same name and values. It replaces the earlier 'appearance' prop (default/subtle/inline), which is deprecated but still accepted: subtle and inline both map to context=inline, default to context=default. The old code-only appearance=inline look (subtle without the hover background) was merged into context=inline, so Key Value Pair inline fields now get Figma's hover background.
isInvalid renders with strokeWeight=2 even when not focused, confirmed directly from node data - invalid's thicker border is not a focus-only effect.

Figma's literal focus treatment thickens the frame's own border 1px->2px and swaps its color to --color-border-focus. Focus/typing replaces the resting border's color directly - the same pattern invalid already uses - rather than adding an outline ring around it, per explicit design feedback. Border width does not literally change to 2px, though: an earlier pass changed the real border-width on context=default's focus AND invalid, matching Figma directly, but that shifts the content box (and the placeholder/value text and typing caret) on every side, reported directly against the component from a side-by-side screenshot - both now paint the extra pixel via box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 calc(var(--border-width-md) - var(--border-width-sm)) <color> instead, keeping border-width a constant 1px in the box model with zero layout impact.

Hover is suppressed once the field is focus/typing (:focus-within, or the pinned data-force-state='focus' reference) - hover should only ever be visible on an inactive field, per explicit design feedback.

showCaret and placeholder (BOOLEAN) component properties exist only to drive Figma's own mockup and have no code equivalent - a real input shows its own caret and switches placeholder/value automatically.

context=inline's bottom corners are always square (border-bottom-{left,right}-radius: 0), confirmed directly from Figma's per-corner radius data on the inline variants - only the top corners share context=default's radius.

context=inline rests at the same 1px bottom border-width context=default uses at rest, per explicit design feedback (an earlier pass reserved a constant 2px transparent border specifically to avoid a layout shift; that reservation was reverted). Reverting it reintroduced the shift a real border-width change causes (the vertically-centered text visibly nudges by a pixel), so focus/invalid on context=inline now paint the thicker look via box-shadow (inset 0 calc(-1 * (var(--border-width-md) - var(--border-width-sm))) 0 0 <color>) instead, keeping border-bottom-width a constant 1px in the box model at every state - zero layout impact. context=default uses the same technique, inset on all four sides.

Neither `.root[data-invalid='true']` nor `.context_inline[data-invalid='true']` touches border-width: both paint the thicker error line with an inset box-shadow (four-sided on context=default, bottom-only on context=inline), so there is no leftover border-width shorthand to reset and no text shift.

Hovering an invalid context=inline field keeps the error border color rather than resetting to --color-border-input, per explicit design feedback - the border-color-changing hover rule is scoped with :not([data-invalid='true']); the background-changing hover rule is not, since hover should still tint the background on an invalid field.

elemBeforeInput and elemAfterInput are separate, asymmetric Figma components (icon|text vs icon-button|button), not a symmetric before/after pair - iconBefore is always aria-hidden, iconAfter is never forced aria-hidden.
Inline padding is asymmetric per size (tighter on the end side) and the icon/input gap varies per size (4px/6px/8px) rather than a flat 6px, confirmed directly from Figma's per-side bound variables.

elemAfterInput gained a third `type` option in Figma - `label` - alongside `icon` and `button`, nesting a real Label atom instance (tone=default, emphasis=subtle, size sm/md). Since `iconAfter` is already `React.ReactNode` and `.action` is a plain centered flex wrapper, this required no component code change - only documenting the newly-supported content type.

Gained an additive leadingContent slot so Select can render multi-select chips inside the field frame without a second bordered frame or duplicated state CSS. In-frame, before the input, not aria-hidden (unlike the decorative iconBefore); shrinks/clips to keep the field single-line. Additive and opt-in - existing TextField usage is unchanged. Not derived from a TextField Figma variant; it exists to serve Select, whose own select-trigger nests chips inside its text-field instance.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.description: Stacks the label, control, and message in one column.

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.description: Quiet form label at --typography-heading-xxs, --color-content-subtle. Points at the control's id, and its own id is the control's aria-labelledby. Omitted when label is not provided.

anatomy.name: required
anatomy.description: Decorative '*' after the label when required, --color-content-error. The forwarded native required conveys the state to assistive technology.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.description: The wrapped control (the slot), cloned to receive id / aria-labelledby / aria-describedby / aria-invalid / required, plus context='inline' when Field's context='inline' (so the control renders borderless/inline). Rendered at the container's edge; only label/message indent in the inline context.

anatomy.name: message
anatomy.description: Helper/error/success line at --typography-body-sm, linked to the control via aria-describedby. Omitted when message is not provided.

anatomy.name: messageIcon
anatomy.description: Decorative sm status Icon shown on error (status_error) / success (status_success) only. Aligned to the message's first line: the message row aligns to the top (align-items: flex-start), and the icon's box is one body-sm line tall (--typography-body-sm-line-height) with the icon centered in it, so a wrapped message keeps the icon beside line one.

children.description: The single control to wrap. Must be one React element - it is cloned to receive the accessibility wiring.

label.description: Label text, rendered in a real native label[htmlFor]; the control also gets aria-labelledby naming it, unless it has its own aria-label or aria-labelledby. Omit only when the control is labelled another way; then no label is rendered.

message.description: Helper/error/success text below the control, linked via aria-describedby. Colour and status icon follow state.

state.description: Colours the message and prepends a status icon; error also sets aria-invalid on the control. Does not set the control's own error border. `valid` is the deprecated name for `success` and renders the same.

context.description: default aligns label/message with the control's outer edge (size-independent). inline indents them to the control's inner text and gives the control context='inline' unless it sets its own - meant for text-bearing controls (Text Field, Select, Text Area, pickers), not Checkbox/Switch/Radio.

size.description: Matches the wrapped control's size. Consumed ONLY in the inline context, to align the label/message with the control's inner text (lg indents more; sm and md share one). No visual effect in the default context. Never resizes the control.

required.description: Shows a decorative '*' after the label and forwards required to the control.

controlId.description: Explicit id for the control, used for the label's htmlFor and the message's aria-describedby. Auto-generated when omitted; a control with its own id keeps it.

className.description: Composes with the root element's class list.

labelClassName.description: Composes with the label's class list.

messageClassName.description: Composes with the message's class list.

layout.messageIconBlockSize: --typography-body-sm-line-height (one message line, so the icon sits on the first line of a wrapped message)

requirements: The label is a real label[htmlFor] pointing at the control's id (generated when the control has none), so the control gets its accessible name from the label - no aria-label on the control.

The label also has an id, which Field passes to the control as aria-labelledby unless the control has its own aria-label or aria-labelledby, so a control htmlFor can't reach (Rich Text Area's div editor, Date Time Picker's group) is named too.
The message is linked to the control via aria-describedby, merged with any aria-describedby the control already carries.
state='error' sets aria-invalid on the control; an explicit control aria-invalid always wins.
required forwards native required to the control; the visible '*' is aria-hidden.

Field only fills in wiring the control left unset - the control's own id/aria-labelledby/aria-invalid/aria-describedby/required/context (or deprecated appearance/tone) are never overwritten, and a control's own aria-label keeps Field from adding aria-labelledby.
Use Field for one control only; a group of controls needs fieldset/legend instead of a single label[htmlFor].

subParts.name: code-parts / <label>
subParts.note: Figma code-part for the label. Axes context x size, plus a showRequired boolean and a labelText string. Rendered in code as Field's own native <label>, NOT the Label atom (this part is heading/xxs on color/content/subtle with no background; the Label atom is a pill with overline typography and a background).

subParts.name: code-parts / <message>
subParts.note: Figma code-part for the message. Axes error x valid x context x size. error -> status_error icon + color/content/error; valid -> status_success icon + color/content/success; neither -> no icon, color/content/subtle. Rendered in code as Field's own message, NOT the Inline Message molecule (this part is a compact sm icon + body/sm line with only default/error/valid states; Inline Message is larger, tone-based, and sometimes interactive).

slot.note: The <field> root exposes a Figma slot for the control - mapped to React children.

apiAdaptationNotes: Field renders its own label and message rather than reusing the Label atom / Inline Message molecule - the Figma <label>/<message> code-parts use different typography (heading/xxs, body/sm) and a smaller state set (default/error/valid) than those components expose.

Figma's 'state' axis (default/error/valid) drives the label/message layer and aria-invalid only. It deliberately does not paint the control's own error border, because Field can't know the control's styling prop name - consumers pair state='error' with the control's own invalid prop. Select, Date Picker, Time Picker, Date Time Picker, and Rich Text Area treat an incoming aria-invalid as invalid, so their border follows, and Slider and Slider Range show their error colors for it; Text Field and Text Area need invalid.

Figma's 'context' (default/inline) and 'size' axes are coupled and reduce to a start-padding indent on the label and message: 0 in default; the control's own inner start padding in inline (lg -> --spacing-md, sm/md -> --spacing-sm), confirmed directly from the <label>/<message> bound variables. Figma models this as one size=all variant for the default context and separate size=lg / size=sm/md variants for inline - i.e. size only distinguishes anything in the inline context. Both contexts keep the same vertical stack. The code keeps a plain sm|md|lg size prop but consumes it only via .context_inline.size_* rules, so the default context stays size-independent.

The inline indent aligns the label/message to a control's inner text, so context='inline' is intended for text-bearing controls (Text Field, Select, Text Area, pickers); it has no meaningful effect on controls without inner text (Checkbox, Switch, Radio). size matches the wrapped control's size and selects the inline indent; it does not resize the control (set the control's own size too).

context is a single shared axis in Figma (the same 'context' property, default/inline, sits on <field>, text-field, text-area, select, etc.), so Field propagates context='inline' to the control by injecting context='inline' - Text Field, Text Area, and Select take the same context prop with the same values. The control's own context (or a deprecated appearance/tone) wins. This is deliberately unlike state (which maps to the control's separate isInvalid axis and stays consumer-set).
The required '*' is decorative (aria-hidden) - the forwarded native 'required' conveys the requirement to assistive technology, avoiding a doubled announcement.

Accessibility wiring is injected by cloning the single child control and only filling in props it left unset (id, aria-labelledby naming the label unless the control has its own aria-label or aria-labelledby, aria-describedby merged with any existing value, aria-invalid, required, data-force-state) - the same React.cloneElement pattern Inline Edit uses. The control's own props always win.

The label has an id as well as htmlFor, and Field passes that id to the control as aria-labelledby, because htmlFor only names a labelable native element. That is what names Rich Text Area's contenteditable div and Date Time Picker's group.

Every form control in the system forwards the wiring: Text Field and Text Area spread it onto the native input/textarea; Select, Date Picker, and Time Picker pass aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, aria-invalid, and required to their input, not the wrapper; Rich Text Area sets them on its editor (required as aria-required); Date Time Picker names its group with the label, keeps the description on the group, and passes the error and required to both inputs; Slider spreads it onto its range input; Slider Range names its group with the label, takes the id as its lower handle's, and passes the description, the error, and required to both handles.
The message icon->text gap is Figma spacing/075 (6px), --spacing-075.

Figma's `valid` (the <field> state axis and the <message> boolean) is `success` in code since 2026-10-22, the name every message component uses (shared-value-names). `valid` is still accepted as a deprecated alias and renders the same (data-state='success').

examples.description: The native disabled attribute: the switch can't be changed and leaves the tab order.

examples.name: Loading
examples.description: isLoading shows a Spinner in the track and ignores toggles while a change is saved; the switch stays focusable and sets aria-busy.

examples.name: Controlled, saving the change
examples.description: Keep the value in your state and set isLoading while the change saves, so the switch stays focused and can't be flipped twice.

examples.name: Icons hidden
examples.description: showIcons={false} draws a plain track without the check and X marks; the loading Spinner shows either way.

examples.name: Small
examples.description: size="sm" is a 32 by 16px track with a smaller label; md, the default, is 40 by 20px.

antiExamples.name: Label written as an instruction

antiExamples.name: Disabling the switch while the change saves
antiExamples.reason: It drops out of the tab order, so keyboard focus is lost, and it reads as unavailable. Set isLoading while the change saves.

anatomy.description: bordered, rounded box with the tone's tinted background and colored border

anatomy.name: icon
anatomy.description: the status icon for the tone, in its status color; decorative

anatomy.name: title
anatomy.description: optional bold lead line (heading-sm)

anatomy.name: description
anatomy.description: the children; wraps to multiple lines (body-md). Required unless errors is set

anatomy.name: errors
anatomy.description: optional list from errors: one bulleted line per field, a Link to #targetId then what to do

anatomy.name: actions
anatomy.description: optional actions (typically Link Buttons), laid out by a ButtonGroup the caller passes; no separators are injected

anatomy.name: dismiss
anatomy.description: optional dismiss IconButton (xs, subtle) in the top-right

statusLabel.default: the tone's name (Information, Success, Warning, Error)
statusLabel.description: Visually hidden text read before the message, since the status icon is decorative. An empty string omits it.

title.description: Optional bold title above the description.

children.description: The description. Wraps to multiple lines. Required unless errors lists what's wrong.

errors.type: Array<{ label: React.ReactNode; message?: React.ReactNode; targetId: string }>
errors.description: The fields that need fixing, for a form's summary after a failed submit. Listed under the description; each label is a Link to #targetId that moves focus to the control (or the first control inside a target that can't take focus).

actions.description: Optional actions (typically Link Buttons). Wrap multiple in a ButtonGroup, which lays them out as a row; a single action can be passed bare.

dismissLabel.description: Accessible name for the dismiss button.

onDismiss.description: Called when dismissed. The message also hides itself.

role.description: Overridable ARIA role - e.g. alert for urgent errors.

spacing.actionsGap: --spacing-sm (the ButtonGroup between the actions owns this; the .actions wrapper matches it for bare actions)

accessibility.statusAnnounced: Visually hidden statusLabel before the title.
accessibility.errorsList: errors renders a ul; each link moves focus to its control (or the first control inside it) and prevents the in-page jump.

figmaSource.notes: Figma boolean properties (title, actions, isDismissible) map to optional props in code (title/actions omitted to hide; isDismissible defaults false). The Figma `discovery` tone was removed by the designer; code ships information/success/warning/error. Actions are Link Button instances laid out in a Button Group (the designer replaced the earlier middot-separated Links with a button-group instance; verified 2026-09-09).
